Convert pSI output to gene lists

Source: R/pSI.list.R
pSI.list.Rd

pSI.list extracts, for each cell type/sample and each of the four standard pSI thresholds (0.05, 0.01, 0.001 and 0.0001), the genes whose pSI values fall below the threshold, i.e. the genes specific to that cell type.

Usage

pSI.list(pSIs, write.csv = FALSE)

Arguments

pSIs

data frame output from specificity.index, with one column per cell type/sample and genes as rows.

write.csv

logical. If TRUE, one CSV file per threshold (pSi_0.05.csv, pSi_0.01.csv, pSi_0.001.csv, pSi_1e-04.csv) is written to the current working directory. The default is FALSE: since pSI 1.2.0 nothing is written unless you ask for it.

Value

A named list of four data frames (pSi_0.0001, pSi_0.001, pSi_0.01, pSi_0.05), one per pSI threshold. Each has one column per cell type/sample, named <sample>_<threshold>, containing the symbols of the genes with pSI below that threshold, padded with NA.

Details

Gene symbols are converted to upper case for consistency in downstream analysis. Within each data frame the columns hold different numbers of genes and are padded with NA to equal length.

See also

pSI.count for the counts alone, candidate.overlap to intersect these lists with a candidate gene list.

Author

Xiaoxiao Xu, Alan B. Wells, David R. O'Brien, Arye Nehorai, Joseph D. Dougherty

Examples

##load sample pSI output
data(sample.data)
##List the genes specific to each cell type/sample type across all pSI thresholds
pSI.out.list <- pSI.list(pSIs=sample.data$pSI.output)
names(pSI.out.list)
#> [1] "pSi_0.0001" "pSi_0.001"  "pSi_0.01"   "pSi_0.05"  
head(pSI.out.list$pSi_0.01)
